title: Tu me manques ou je manque de temps ?
summary: Distinguish emotional absence, a missed event, a lack and failure to fulfil a commitment.
objectives: Use manquer à with the missed person or thing as subject.
Distinguish manquer + object from manquer de + resource.
Interpret manquer à an obligation without assuming every à marks emotional missing.

sources.label: Public A2 index: topic-coverage reference only

sections.title: The person missed becomes the French subject
paragraphs: For emotional missing, manquer à someone describes what is absent from that person's life. In tu me manques, tu is the missed person and me is the person feeling the absence: I miss you. The verb agrees with the missed person or thing, not the person experiencing the feeling. In English the experiencer comes first; in French the grammatical roles are different.

Replace à + experiencer with me, te, lui, nous, vous, leur before the verb. Lui can mean to him or to her. A full noun can follow à: sa famille manque à Nora. The same construction works in the past: tu m'as manqué.
points: Present manquer: je manque, tu manques, il/elle/on manque, nous manquons, vous manquez, ils/elles manquent.
For I miss them, use ils/elles me manquent. For they miss me, use je leur manque.

examples.note: The speaker is the person being missed.
A place can be what is missed.

mistakes.why: The plural subject is mes amis, not me.

sections.title: A direct object, de or à changes the relationship
paragraphs: Manquer + direct object can mean miss an event, appointment, transport or target: manquer le train. Manquer de + noun means lack a resource or quality: manquer de temps, de patience. Something missing from a set can itself be the subject: il manque une page, une page manque au dossier.

Manquer à also has a non-emotional use with an obligation: manquer à sa promesse means fail to keep one's promise. The complement's meaning matters; à is not an automatic signal for a person feeling emotional absence. Manquer de + infinitive can mean nearly do something, such as j'ai manqué de tomber; recognise this separately from lacking a noun resource.
points: Useful contrast: j'ai manqué le cours = I missed the class; le cours m'a manqué = I missed having the class / felt its absence, depending on context.

examples.note: A missed departure takes a direct object.

examples.english: One page is missing from the application.
examples.note: Impersonal il introduces what is missing.

examples.english: He failed to keep his promise.

mistakes.avoid: Nous manquons du temps pour finir.
mistakes.prefer: Nous manquons de temps pour finir.
mistakes.why: For an unspecified shortage, manquer de takes the noun without a partitive article.

sections.title: Say who is short of a particular amount
paragraphs: Il me manque ... combines the impersonal subject il with an indirect pronoun for the person experiencing a practical shortage. The thing or amount missing follows the verb: il nous manque deux pièces. This is not the emotional pattern where the missed person or thing becomes the subject.

Manquer de describes a general shortage without a partitive article. Impersonal il manque introduces what is absent and can retain a determiner: il manque une vis, il manque du matériel. Une vis (feminine) is a screw; le matériel (masculine) is equipment.
points: Keep manque singular after impersonal il, even when several missing objects follow it.

examples.french: **Il nous manque trois planches** pour finir l'étagère.
examples.english: We are three boards short of finishing the shelf.
examples.note: The missing amount is specified; il is the grammatical subject.

examples.french: Nous **manquons de matériel** ; **il manque du matériel** dans cette caisse.
examples.english: We lack equipment; there is equipment missing from this crate.
examples.note: Different constructions explain de versus du.

practice.prompt: Supply manquer in the present: Tu me ___.
In Je lui manque, who feels the absence?
Supply de or à: Nous manquons ___ place.
Supply manquer in the passé composé: Elle ___ son rendez-vous.
practice.explanation: A missed appointment is a direct object.

practice.prompt: Translate 'I miss my sisters' using mes sœurs as the subject and manquer.
practice.explanation: The missed people become the subject.

practice.prompt: Translate 'My parents miss me' with je as subject and leur.
practice.explanation: Je is missed; leur represents the parents experiencing it.

practice.prompt: Supply manquer in the passé composé: Tu m'___ pendant le voyage.
practice.explanation: The construction remains the same in the past.

practice.prompt: Replace à Nora: Sa famille ___ manque.
Supply the missing noun-linking preposition: Il manque ___ patience.

choices: The bus felt sad without me.
practice.explanation: The direct object gives the missed transport meaning.

practice.prompt: Supply à or de: Elle a manqué ___ sa parole.
practice.explanation: Manquer à sa parole means fail to keep one's word.

practice.prompt: Present of manquer: Il ___ deux signatures sur ce formulaire.
practice.explanation: Impersonal il keeps a singular verb even though two signatures are absent.

practice.prompt: Translate 'We miss you' using tu as subject and nous.
Correct the quantity phrase only: Nous manquons des chaises. We lack chairs in general.
practice.explanation: Use de without an indefinite article.

practice.prompt: Present of manquer: Vos messages me ___.

practice.explanation: Manquer de + infinitive can express a narrowly avoided event.

practice.prompt: Replace à nos collègues with the indirect pronoun, keeping the impersonal construction: Il manque deux outils à nos collègues.
practice.explanation: Leur names the people short of tools; impersonal il keeps singular manque.

practice.prompt: Choose de or du for a general resource shortage: Nous manquons ___ bois. Then choose de or du for the impersonal construction: Il manque ___ bois dans la réserve. Give the two answers separated by a comma.
practice.explanation: Manquer de takes bare de before the resource, whereas impersonal il manque can introduce a partitive du bois.

production_task.prompt: Write to a friend after moving. Express what you miss, explain a practical shortage and mention an appointment or bus you missed.
production_task.model_answer: Tu me manques, et nos promenades me manquent aussi. Ici, je manque encore de temps pour découvrir le quartier. Hier, j'ai manqué le bus, mais j'ai trouvé un autre trajet.
production_task.translation: I miss you, and I miss our walks too. Here, I am still short of time to discover the neighbourhood. Yesterday, I missed the bus, but I found another route.
rubric: Make the missed person or thing the subject for emotional absence.
Use de for a lack of a resource.
Use a direct object for missing transport.
